item.title: Irish PM Micheal Martin pushes Trump on Iran war — politely
item.description: The 65-year-old Taoiseach begs to differ with US President Trump on issues from Iran war to migration to ties with British PM Starmer.

item.title: US House Committee subpoenas Attorney General Pam Bondi over Epstein files
item.description: Committee examines compliance with law governing disclosure of Epstein files.

item.title: Iran confirms assassination of Ali Larijani in Israeli attack
item.description: Iran's Supreme National Security Council confirms assassination of its chief Ali Larijani, his son and bodyguards in Israeli air strike.

item.title: Over 200 Ukrainian experts deploy to Middle East to counter Iranian drones — Zelenskyy
item.description: Ukrainian president says teams deployed at request of partners, including the United States.

item.title: CAF strips Senegal of latest AFCON title, declares Morocco champions
item.description: Following a dramatic walk-off by Senegal in the January final, CAF rules the match a forfeit, recording a 3-0 victory in favour of the Moroccan side.

item.title: Ali Larijani: The 'Man of the Moment' who bridged Iran's old guard and new era
item.description: Veteran politician held top roles in Iran’s security, media and legislative institutions over four decades.

item.title: UK adviser judged Iran nuclear deal was within reach just before war began — report
item.description: Diplomats say progress in talks suggested diplomatic path remained open.

item.title: Iran vows revenge for security chief Larijani's assassination
item.description: "Iran's response to the assassination of the secretary of the Supreme National Security Council will be decisive and regrettable," Iran's army chief says.

item.title: Iraq's KRG, Baghdad agree to resume oil exports via Türkiye's Ceyhan port amid Hormuz disruption
item.description: The deal to restart the northern pipeline comes as the closure of the Strait of Hormuz during the war on Iran continues to rattle global energy markets and push prices higher.

item.title: Nearly 90 vessels transit Strait of Hormuz as Iran continues to export oil despite war
item.description: Despite most traffic through the crucial Strait of Hormuz being halted since early March, Iran has still exported over 16 million barrels of oil since the war began.
